page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.12xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized server instance designed around the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. Driven by a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor, the configuration provides 48 virtual CPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system includes 96.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. This configuration prioritizes execution frequency and dense core allocation over massive memory capacity, targeting tasks that depend primarily on CPU cycle availability.

The instance does not include integrated local solid-state storage, requiring instances to interface with network-attached block storage for file systems and data persistence. Network performance is provisioned with a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth, offering high-throughput connectivity to handle remote storage operations and distributed node communication. The instance does not feature graphical processing units or specialized hardware acceleration, keeping host resource distribution focused entirely on general x86 instruction processing.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 core-to-memory profile makes the c8ib.12xlarge efficient for workloads where additional RAM would remain unutilized. The high baseline networking helps mitigate the absence of local storage by supporting rapid access to remote storage services and low-latency cluster messaging. This server type fits compute-bound applications, including continuous integration and build pipelines, distributed batch jobs, video encoding, financial simulations, and high-throughput application servers.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ib.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance supplies 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with dedicated allocation, paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no integrated local storage, directing all storage input and output over network interfaces, which are supported by a high-throughput 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without integrated hardware accelerators or GPUs, hardware resources are directed toward raw x86 compute throughput. This architectural balance between high-frequency CPU cores and robust interconnect capacity provides efficient density for compute-bound tasks, avoiding the cost of excess memory overhead. The c8ib.12xlarge is suitable for computational modeling, media transcoding, scientific batch processing, and distributed microservices that demand substantial processor cycles and high inter-node communication.
